description:
FOUND s499a (Opus, 2026-09-27, measurement only), ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/REPORT.md.

MECHANISM (read): %p-fasl-cache-enabled-p (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) answers NIL while *pcl-fasl-build* is bound, and %p-ext-fasl-enabled-p the same, so while compile-file builds the MAIN SCRIPT's fasl (p-run-script-cached step 3) every `use` the program runs at compile time loads that module from its cached TEXT -- `load` of source, SBCL's native compiler on every top-level form -- although the module's valid FASL is sitting in the cache.  The docstring's reason (no compile-file nested inside compile-file) is about a module fasl that must be BUILT; loading an EXISTING one compiles nothing.  PCL_FASL_DEBUG shows it: `module Local.pm -> TEXT`, `extension pcl-pack -> TEXT` under a `script ... -> fasl-build` line.

MEASURED (experiment, nothing shipped): ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/bin/exp-fasl-in-build2.lisp encapsulates both predicates to answer as if *pcl-fasl-build* were unbound (all module fasls warm), injected by a COPY of pcl (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/bin/pcl-phase).  Cold script run = program source touched, modules warm; interleaved ctl/exp/ctl2, min of 3 (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/exp1.log, exp1b.log):
  real-dir-walker 8.33 -> 0.50 s (build 7.95 -> 0.11)
  File-Path-Find 5.94 -> 0.36;  Getopt-Long 5.33 -> 0.34;  Time-Local 5.56 -> 0.31 (the pcl-pack EXTENSION, 4+ s, is the TEXT load there);  local-time-format 5.53 -> 0.35;  Data-Dumper 2.24 -> 0.27;  JSON-PP 4.27 -> 1.15;  posix-funcs 1.24 -> 0.32;  moo-class 4.60 -> 3.06.
  Whole everyday corpus, K=1 (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/exp1-all.log): 84.8 s -> 37.3 s (-56 %), 27 of 101 programs save > 0.2 s, stdout identical 101/101 in both arms.
  Rosetta first runs (no experiment, phase log): the script BUILD is 280 s of 470 s total over 499 programs; the worst are `use bigint`/Math::* programs at 10-11.5 s build each (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/s499a/rosetta-times.tsv first_build_s).
WHO PAYS: the first run of every program, EVERY run after an edit, and every run from a new cwd (the script key carries the cwd).  Warm runs are unaffected.
QUESTIONS FOR THE FIXER: the fasl was built with *pcl-fasl-build* bound (BEGIN moved to load time) -- confirm loading it inside the outer compile-file gives the module's compile-time effects the reader needs (#1844's first-run silent wrong is the hazard class; the 101/101 identical outputs above are the evidence so far); a MISSING module fasl must still load from text (never a nested build).

=== NOTE (s510f, s512) ===
#2702 removed this cost as a side effect: a first run now runs the program's TEXT, so its modules load the ordinary way (FASL HIT when their compiled files exist) and the build at exit finds them loaded.  Measured 2026-10-07: a Getopt::Long script's first run 3.6 -> 0.22 s, a 60-line script 1.5 -> 0.56 s.  What remains is a large script's own compile (1026 lines: 6.6 -> 7.1 s).
subject: PERF (first run after an edit): a script's fasl BUILD loads every `use`d module and extension from TEXT even when its fasl exists -- Getopt::Long 5.3 s -> 0.34 s cold, the everyday corpus's first runs 84.8 s -> 37.3 s with the fasl reused
